papers.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
papers.abstract: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$. Applied to a Poisson bivector, this produces a Poisson bivector, extending Bottacin's structure from surfaces to arbitrary dimension. Applied to a top degree polyvector $s$ and wedged with a transverse Euler frame, it produces an anticanonical section on $M$, which we call the \emph{leafrian}. When $X$ is a Poisson surface, we prove that the leafrian splits the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons if and only if $s$ Frobenius-splits the base. The mechanism itself is dimension-free. The construction also recovers and generalizes the splittings of the Lie-theoretic examples: the $r$-matrix need not satisfy the classical Yang--Baxter equation.

papers.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
papers.abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.

papers.title: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
papers.abstract: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).

papers.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
papers.abstract: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.

papers.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
papers.abstract: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.

papers.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
papers.abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.

papers.title: A K\"unneth theorem for the cyclic homology of A-infinity algebras
papers.abstract: The cyclic homology of a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, smooth and proper $A_\infty$ category satisfying the Hodge-to-de-Rham degeneration property carries the structure of a polarized semi-infinite Hodge structure or the so-called EP-structure. Given two $A_\infty$ algebras $A$ and $B$ with the above conditions, we construct a K\"unneth map from the tensor product of their cyclic homologies to the cyclic homology of the $A_\infty$ tensor product $A\otimes_\infty B$ and show that it respects the EP-structures. As an application, we show that if $A$ and $B$ are equipped with weak Calabi-Yau structures, then $A\otimes_\infty B$ also inherits a weak Calabi-Yau structure. Also, we show that the K\"unneth quasi-isomorphism respects good splittings of the Hodge filtration on $A$ and $B$ compatible with the weak Calabi-Yau structure. Our explicit calculations rely on the combinatorial (tree) description of the tensor product of $A_\infty$ algebras developed in \cite{amorim2016tensor}.
